runs.entry: Price **$287.32** (quote of 2026-10-16 printed by `tools/run.py`, aggregator, flagged). Shares **168,910,851**, one class (10-Q for the quarter ended 2026-06-30, filed 2026-07-22, accession 0001628280-26-049139, cover as of 2026-07-17; `cover_shares.py`; checked against 171.9M issued less 2.8M treasury = 169.1M at 2026-06-30, the difference the buyback; after the 10-Q only the 8-K of 2026-10-01, accession 0000943452-26-000013, a commercial paper programme of up to $2.0 billion with nothing issued); cap **$48,532M**. Sovereign **5.43%** (US Treasury daily par yield curve, 30-year, 2026-10-15). Filings read: 10-K FY2025 (0001628280-26-008067), 10-Q Q2 2026, DEF 14A filed 2026-03-31 (0001628280-26-022197), 8-Ks 2026-07-22 and 2026-10-01, 10-Ks FY2018 and FY2020 to FY2024 for the cycle; one figure cross-checked (2025 operating cash $1,759M on the filed statement against the tool's 1,759, 2023 likewise). Lines of evidence derived by the analyst from the 10-K's Items 1, 1A and 7 (the brief's departure), fourteen lines listed in Step 0 with their source. The 10-K names Knorr-Bremse (with New York Air Brake), Amsted Rail, Progress Rail of Caterpillar and CRRC; Caterpillar the only SEC filer among them, read from its 10-Ks FY2019, FY2022 and FY2025 (Progress Rail not reported apart); the others flagged as non-filers. **Q1 IN**: Freight decides (78.7% of segment operating income 2021 to 2025, $5,635M against Transit $1,524M), foreseeable in a range from an installed base of nearly 24,600 locomotives and about 60% aftermarket sales. **Q2 IN**: one of two North American locomotive makers with certification barriers; gross margin 28.3% (2020), 30.3%, 30.4%, 30.4%, rising to 34.1% (2025) through the inflation; Freight margin 11.8% to 11.5% through the 2020 downturn; pre-tax returns on net tangible capital 68% to 114% 2019 to 2025; Caterpillar's segment holding Progress Rail 13.8% to 19.9% against Wabtec Freight 11.5% to 19.5% 2017 to 2025; Progress Rail's suit alleging Wabtec monopolized the market, antitrust claims dismissed 2025, all settled 2026 without admission; the 10-K's own line that price competition 'has historically limited our ability to increase prices' the strongest fact against, carried to Q7. **Q3 WEIGHS FOR** on the business (little tangible capital, growth needing little more), **AGAINST** on the bought growth (about 13.2% pre-tax on total capital including goodwill in 2025; Inspection Technologies $1.788B and Frauscher $792M bought mostly for goodwill and intangibles, Dellner $1,062M in 2026, earnings undisclosed, 'not significant'). **Q4 IN**, no confusion or suspicion; ten balance sheets 2016 to 2025 read (the 2019 GE Transportation merger paid mainly in shares took goodwill to $8.4B; 2025 acquisitions took debt from $4.0B to $5.5B; a $3.3B non-cash retained-earnings reduction on retiring 55M treasury shares; inventory to 24.6% of sales with customer deposits rising beside it); **WEIGHS AGAINST** on featured adjusted EPS, reconciled EBITDA and an EBITDA-based pay metric. **Q5 integrity IN** (the 2018 Justice Department no-poach consent decree with Knorr-Bremse, under the earlier leadership, the strongest fact against; that era's chairman leaving the board in 2026); ability **WEIGHS FOR**. **Q6 WEIGHS AGAINST** (buybacks since 2024 of $1.79B at $160 to $263 a share, well above the bottom of the range; acquisitions mostly goodwill with undisclosed earnings; the 2025 bonus raised by committee from 178.1% to 192.8% of target for tariffs). Owner cash (operating cash less the cash-flow stock-pay add-back less depreciation as the maintenance guess, interest added back after the company's own tax) **$1,276.3M** a year before interest on the literal window 2021 to 2025 (maintenance case, central), **$1,290.5M** all spending, **$1,124.4M** after interest; net purchases $3,827M over the window exceed half of owner cash, so **serial acquirer**, central figure the organic pair at the filer's organic growth of 8.78% a year, the default pair beside (growth cut to 9.31% under specific (f)). **Q7 OUT**: value **$104.21 to $245.51** a share (all-equity, organic pair, maintenance case, 5.43%, net debt $5,901M at 2026-06-30) against **$287.32**; expected return 2.34% to 4.80%, no case earns the floor, the price above the top of every range; all-spending $105.76 to $248.63, default pair $104.21 to $201.86, equity-only $122.59 to $247.07 beside. Fair **$72.20** all-equity (central), **$94.39** equity-only. Facts after the stop, not weighed: debt $6,571M gross at 2026-06-30 ($1,656M current) against cash $670M; principal $1,250M due 2026 and $1,840M 2027 to 2028; covenants interest coverage at least 3.0 and net leverage at most 3.5; operating income about 8 times net interest in 2025; BBB / Baa2 / BBB stable; guarantees and letters of credit $1,141M; asbestos not estimable; Kazakhstan/CIS sales $431M with sanctions risk named. Contamination declared by the analyst: the session's opening git status and commit subjects naming the R run and its fold, and a memory index line about queue state; a Test Runs listing filtered for this ticker only, nothing found; none used. Commits 310039c4, 697d60b7, ddb6f7e8, 7c47fef1, 3a8a35e9, aee534f1, 68b10c8f (write-early kept, Q3 and Q4 committed together, confessed in the self-audit). Position note filled at the fold: not held. Citations: the analyst's check clean (109 ids, 28 quoted fragments); the dispatcher's `dispatcher_cite_check.py` 109 ids, 25 quoted cites, no missing id, no E-id, no slip. No tracked research file over 200 KB. check_framework PASS. **For the operator:** the analyst's gaps: (1) Q4 and EBITDA reconciled in releases and used in pay but not presented as earnings in the accounts, STOP or weighing (read as a weighing); (2) the serial-acquirer test's owner cash before purchases does not say before or after interest (met on both); (3) purchases closing late in the window put their whole price in net debt and almost none of their earnings in the base, and whether a disclosed price with undisclosed earnings is treated as a deal with no filed record; (4) whether past buybacks are read against today's bottom of the range or the bottom as it stood then. Could not get: the earnings of Inspection Technologies, Frauscher and Dellner; Caterpillar's rail-only profit and any figure for the non-filing rivals; the outcome of the Siemens antitrust counterclaims of 2018; whether the shares given for GE Transportation were worth less than what was received (left undecided).
runs.narr: OUT at Q7 after Q1 IN (Freight 78.7% of segment operating income 2021 to 2025, an installed base of nearly 24,600 locomotives, about 60% aftermarket), Q2 IN (one of two North American locomotive makers, certification barriers, gross margin 28.3% to 34.1% 2020 to 2025 through the inflation, pre-tax returns on net tangible capital 68% to 114%, Progress Rail of Caterpillar not displacing it; the 10-K's line that price competition has limited price rises against), Q3 for the business and against the bought growth, Q4 IN with featured adjusted EPS and an EBITDA pay metric against, Q5 integrity IN (the 2018 no-poach decree of the earlier leadership the strongest fact against), Q6 against (buybacks of $1.79B since 2024 at $160 to $263, acquisitions mostly goodwill with undisclosed earnings, a bonus raised for tariffs). Owner cash $1,276.3M maintenance case, $1,290.5M all spending, literal window 2021 to 2025, serial acquirer on the organic pair at 8.78%; net debt $5,901M. Value $104.21 to $245.51 against $287.32 at the 5.43% Treasury, expected return 2.3% to 4.8%, no case earning the floor; fair $72.20 all-equity, $94.39 equity-only, armed. Framework gaps for the operator: EBITDA in releases and pay but not the accounts under Q4; owner cash before purchases before or after interest; purchases late in the window; past buybacks against today's bottom of the range.
